title: IO-mode latency frequencies by model & route with trace-sampling playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a concise, operational dashboard and sampling playbook that exposes latency frequency distributions (p50/p95/p99 and full histogram slices) split by model and public route, with a clear streaming vs non-streaming (IO-mode) decomposition. This ticket covers the telemetry plumbing (metrics + traces), the Grafana/Console panels, and a small runbook for on-call to interpret regressions. We also propose a lightweight trace-sampling policy targeted at tail requests to reduce trace volume while preserving investigatability for high-severity incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Console dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model(s) and route(s) with toggle for streaming vs non-streaming
Histogram or frequency heatmap view available to inspect distribution shifts across time windows and by sequence-length cohort
Trace sampling rules implemented: 100% for errors, 5% overall, and additional 10% preferential sampling for requests in top 1% latency tail
Dashboard panels include links to sampled traces and an auto-generated query to fetch relevant logs for the selected cohort
Alerting: SLO breach alert configured for model-route IO-mode slices when p95 exceeds configured threshold for more than 5 minutes
Runbook section added describing triage steps and pointer to known mitigations (fallback model, increased batch size, route routing override)
tasks: Define Prometheus metrics and label schema for io_mode (streaming|blocking), model_family, model_version, route, seq_len_cohort
Add OTLP span attributes for route and io_mode in runtime (trace hook changes)
Implement trace-sampling middleware with priority rules (errors, tail boosts, ad-hoc capture)
Create Console/Grafana panels: p50/p95/p99 timeseries, frequency heatmap, per-route breakdown, sequence-length cohort slicer
Add dashboard links from endpoint detail page to the new dashboard and to sampled traces
Write runbook and add to Console ‘Investigations’ link for on-call
notes: We chose 'io_mode' label to avoid ambiguity with 'streaming' flag present in request payloads; runtime will set io_mode explicitly.
Sequence-length cohorts: 0-64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024. These cohorts will be a derived label in the metrics-exporter to avoid high cardinality at the client side.
Concern: adding model_version label at high cardinality may increase cardinality; plan to support model_family + pinned_version as optional label only for controlled rollout routes.
We'll rely on Tempo (or Beacon) for span storage and link spans in Console panels; if Tempo not available in a private deployment, fall back to local S3-traces index
decisions: Metric backend: use existing Prometheus pushgateway + remote_write to Cortex for long retention; histogram metrics are preferred to gauge-style pXX derivation.
Tracing: OTLP spans with attributes {route, model_family, model_version, io_mode, seq_len_cohort, batch_size}. Sampling to be enforced in the runtime ingress layer.
Sampling policy: base sample rate 5% for successful requests, 100% for errors (status != 200), guaranteed sample of top-1% latency by fast in-process reservoir sampler.
Dashboard: implement in Redwood Console first; create an equivalent Grafana dashboard for infra teams to import.
Alerting: use SLO-based alerts on p95 per (model_family, route, io_mode) with a 5 minute window for flapping suppression.
dashboard_query_snippets:
# PromQL: p95 by route and io_mode
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime"}[5m])) by (le, route, model_family, io_mode))

# Frequency heatmap: bucketed p50/p95 over seq_len cohorts
sum by (seq_len_cohort, route, model_family, io_mode) (rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime"}[5m]))

# Trace link query: traces with tag route=X and io_mode=streaming and duration>p99 threshold
service.name=runtime AND route="<route>" AND io_mode="streaming" AND duration>1000ms
runbook_summary: Step 1: Confirm scope - which model_family and route show p95 > threshold and whether it's isolated to streaming or non-streaming
Step 2: Open the Console panel, apply seq_len_cohort slicer and inspect frequency heatmap to see distribution shift
Step 3: Click through to sampled traces. If KV cache misses are visible in spans, escalate to Serving Runtime team
Step 4: If regression correlates with recent model_version rollout, rollback or pin to previous version
Step 5: If spike is due to sudden request-shape change, consider increasing batch window temporarily and monitor cost impact
